key_insight: This paper argues that robot policies should act in a 3D geometric space, not just on 2D images or latent features, to better handle contact-rich manipulation. By making geometry explicit, the model can reason more reliably about how actions affect objects and the robot in the real world.
problem_solved: Current vision-language-action and video world-action models often rely on 2D frames or 2D-derived representations, which hide the 3D spatial relationships needed for precise robot manipulation. This makes it harder for robots to correctly interpret instructions and execute physically grounded actions.
method: Introduce a geometric action model that incorporates explicit 3D structure into policy learning.
Model interactions among objects, cameras, and robot actions in a physically grounded geometric representation.
Use geometry-aware reasoning to improve action selection for tasks that require contact, positioning, and spatial precision.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a path toward more reliable generalist robot policies that are better at manipulation in real environments. It can improve robustness when tasks depend on depth, pose, and contact dynamics rather than only visual semantics.

paper_title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
paper_authors: Jisang Han, Seonghu Jeon, Jaewoo Jung, René Zurbrügg, Honggyu An
